Keep every row in order. Preserve all [[I]], [[B]], [[SC]] emphasis markers, [[Nnumber]] note markers and explicit source line counts. Do not return hashes; the host binds immutable hashes.", "context": {"title": "David Copperfield", "unit": 62, "heading": "CHAPTER 60. AGNES", "previous_rows": [], "source_language": "English", "part": null, "book": null, "chapter": 60, "role": "chapter"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en85-u062-h", "tag": "h2", "role": "heading", "text": "CHAPTER 60. AGNES", "sha256": "42a71a89131aa013c8e8f5092fbd12966d0df52ff12e2c9e2f4094c916658b3f", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[67]/h2", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": []}, {"id": "en85-u062-b0001", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "My aunt and I, when we were left alone, talked far into the night. How the emigrants never wrote home, otherwise than cheerfully and hopefully; how Mr. Micawber had actually remitted divers small sums of money, on account of those ‘pecuniary liabilities’, in reference to which he had been so business-like as between man and man; how Janet, returning into my aunt’s service when she came back to Dover, had finally carried out her renunciation of mankind by entering into wedlock with a thriving tavern-keeper; and how my aunt had finally set her seal on the same great principle, by aiding and abetting the bride, and crowning the marriage-ceremony with her presence; were among our topics—already more or less familiar to me through the letters I had had. Mr. Dick, as usual, was not forgotten. My aunt informed me how he incessantly occupied himself in copying everything he could lay his hands on, and kept King Charles the First at a respectful distance by that semblance of employment; how it was one of the main joys and rewards of her life that he was free and happy, instead of pining in monotonous restraint; and how (as a novel general conclusion) nobody but she could ever fully know what he was.", "sha256": "bc8fc4c127bb0ff4ef94cb391c85e2db380a7fc5333b65c33fa799505f0003f2", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[67]/p[1]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u062-b0002", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘And when, Trot,’ said my aunt, patting the back of my hand, as we sat in our old way before the fire, ‘when are you going over to Canterbury?’", "sha256": "405e910eddb4a36b412aec1ed83334a5ac11a946db0a533097abea7c0cd480cb", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[67]/p[2]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u062-b0003", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I shall get a horse, and ride over tomorrow morning, aunt, unless you will go with me?’", "sha256": "4753810a7157bf55d690b0438792fec43df5fb037efa5e7ef8019db9f3ca4faa", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[67]/p[3]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u062-b0004", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘No!’ said my aunt, in her short abrupt way. ‘I mean to stay where I am.’", "sha256": "c55a262692cc37af28726646d2ab4f3efe4d83ad693e31f05ee8fca77cfe5e24", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[67]/p[4]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u062-b0005", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Then, I should ride, I said. I could not have come through Canterbury today without stopping, if I had been coming to anyone but her.", "sha256": "5b50c1d65b3b0d2bcc1036be72e9b9f9890af51aedcacbd5ee53b4aa03b02e7a", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[67]/p[5]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u062-b0006", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "She was pleased, but answered, ‘Tut, Trot; MY old bones would have kept till tomorrow!’ and softly patted my hand again, as I sat looking thoughtfully at the fire.", "sha256": "e9bdde62380a54db8d20f991211f586048a2e18b6598d97611d50038c850062a", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[67]/p[6]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u062-b0007", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Thoughtfully, for I could not be here once more, and so near Agnes, without the revival of those regrets with which I had so long been occupied. Softened regrets they might be, teaching me what I had failed to learn when my younger life was all before me, but not the less regrets. ‘Oh, Trot,’ I seemed to hear my aunt say once more; and I understood her better now—‘Blind, blind, blind!’", "sha256": "fd5bea57c7f8575182e2a11d7754c01e9db3d1ff4cdbe171ed3046918a82f791", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[67]/p[7]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u062-b0008", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "We both kept silence for some minutes. When I raised my eyes, I found that she was steadily observant of me. Perhaps she had followed the current of my mind; for it seemed to me an easy one to track now, wilful as it had been once.", "sha256": "328d01d2ccd402242e086f204e3324ff5b19470cb33f04d9c06209c1ef23eebf", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[67]/p[8]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u062-b0009", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘You will find her father a white-haired old man,’ said my aunt, ‘though a better man in all other respects—a reclaimed man. Neither will you find him measuring all human interests, and joys, and sorrows, with his one poor little inch-rule now. Trust me, child, such things must shrink very much, before they can be measured off in that way.’", "sha256": "6ddf013d32f5638962c4f639372d233e51ca970dfb04bd592ccf6a95ddbb8a43", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[67]/p[9]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u062-b0010", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Indeed they must,’ said I.", "sha256": "98d22f7436e93e33c3279442319a618727ba85d1de41d9ac3fd3d6d84b3b7206", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[67]/p[10]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u062-b0011", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘You will find her,’ pursued my aunt, ‘as good, as beautiful, as earnest, as disinterested, as she has always been. If I knew higher praise, Trot, I would bestow it on her.’", "sha256": "952495599f4dd88e979e70e6b5c1ddc6bc18b30547a8b7d5dea736be5e2392cd", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[67]/p[11]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u062-b0012", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "There was no higher praise for her; no higher reproach for me. Oh, how had I strayed so far away!", "sha256": "a05a0c7d3aaf3e1ec702e18f662b850b6d354c0b8575cf560b2ce3619020c80a", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[67]/p[12]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u062-b0013", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘If she trains the young girls whom she has about her, to be like herself,’ said my aunt, earnest even to the filling of her eyes with tears, ‘Heaven knows, her life will be well employed! Useful and happy, as she said that day! How could she be otherwise than useful and happy!’", "sha256": "82bb965dd3f4dd0071e2c863b418ce46d9329cd43d66ed055312fecf81312fc8", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[67]/p[13]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u062-b0014", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Has Agnes any—’ I was thinking aloud, rather than speaking.", "sha256": "7a20dd37441a7e655d57348c8f3e013995a348e6690671cb2d9875f75f882cc6", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[67]/p[14]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u062-b0015", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Well? Hey? Any what?’ said my aunt, sharply.", "sha256": "467ad539e2b6117117a91ad929d54387bbc84ea94a706ed122e161e32d35a223", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[67]/p[15]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u062-b0016", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Any lover,’ said I.", "sha256": "cbc71530b6196943742fcf4771975995a01bdba7153b8d4fcf35f718ba0b6c25", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[67]/p[16]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u062-b0017", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘A score,’ cried my aunt, with a kind of indignant pride. ‘She might have married twenty times, my dear, since you have been gone!’", "sha256": "e770e930fe45f121d687ce0348ef70ce39b04fe3feee3410abb5553f15f2685b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[67]/p[17]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u062-b0018", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘No doubt,’ said I. ‘No doubt. But has she any lover who is worthy of her? Agnes could care for no other.’", "sha256": "b95c836b22543bc4b11a9bf3d879644b1963c55c13707e7892cd618a18fc368e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[67]/p[18]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u062-b0019", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "My aunt sat musing for a little while, with her chin upon her hand. Slowly raising her eyes to mine, she said:", "sha256": "c0a3a3afd6ab549525621dfeef77d1495204f877c97006bae45b95d1353726f4", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[67]/p[19]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u062-b0020", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I suspect she has an attachment, Trot.’", "sha256": "2e726a0861921ba18383734d3a8b33808be9290a577fbbaf8e512c4815eada89", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[67]/p[20]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u062-b0021", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘A prosperous one?’ said I.", "sha256": "5b5c5fad49adcdf62f18497b73e2e7504f61bb1137600e13077d492dcd7b889b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[67]/p[21]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u062-b0022", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Trot,’ returned my aunt gravely, ‘I can’t say. I have no right to tell you even so much. She has never confided it to me, but I suspect it.’", "sha256": "1858a22a1dcde0fe7b4d820f4a66287c37c53629460c9fe82e6b1c3db4058edb", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[67]/p[22]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u062-b0023", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "She looked so attentively and anxiously at me (I even saw her tremble), that I felt now, more than ever, that she had followed my late thoughts. I summoned all the resolutions I had made, in all those many days and nights, and all those many conflicts of my heart.", "sha256": "6f5af8f740e8b2051ef73d4cde3c9322d82b2b487eb5fb55c7c88034ca1cef15", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[67]/p[23]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u062-b0024", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘If it should be so,’ I began, ‘and I hope it is-’", "sha256": "31e79e8caec35838c81c508a452bfdeeb6a0c5e2eed1bf35bdb3779c6578d9fe", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[67]/p[24]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u062-b0025", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I don’t know that it is,’ said my aunt curtly. ‘You must not be ruled by my suspicions. You must keep them secret. They are very slight, perhaps. I have no right to speak.’", "sha256": "7f65b6a6debcdbdfcdaad5728a785fde19cc0af9395f2183f362acba9fb424ad", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[67]/p[25]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u062-b0026", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘If it should be so,’ I repeated, ‘Agnes will tell me at her own good time. A sister to whom I have confided so much, aunt, will not be reluctant to confide in me.’", "sha256": "2a7d543a32c99ba1eea5c8b625abc34dec859512d2a1b1752baff05803ef714a", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[67]/p[26]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u062-b0027", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "My aunt withdrew her eyes from mine, as slowly as she had turned them upon me; and covered them thoughtfully with her hand. By and by she put her other hand on my shoulder; and so we both sat, looking into the past, without saying another word, until we parted for the night.", "sha256": "b103ec4666ab7874e02690bfd172019eb6e4ea67891fa73a863fe638189a492b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[67]/p[27]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u062-b0028", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I rode away, early in the morning, for the scene of my old school-days. I cannot say that I was yet quite happy, in the hope that I was gaining a victory over myself; even in the prospect of so soon looking on her face again.", "sha256": "71f14314dd3f9b5897e9b5bf4bc033e57cccdc35edf2f69ae05c78bd33fab8fd", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[67]/p[28]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u062-b0029", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "The well-remembered ground was soon traversed, and I came into the quiet streets, where every stone was a boy’s book to me. I went on foot to the old house, and went away with a heart too full to enter. I returned; and looking, as I passed, through the low window of the turret-room where first Uriah Heep, and afterwards Mr. Micawber, had been wont to sit, saw that it was a little parlour now, and that there was no office. Otherwise the staid old house was, as to its cleanliness and order, still just as it had been when I first saw it. I requested the new maid who admitted me, to tell Miss Wickfield that a gentleman who waited on her from a friend abroad, was there; and I was shown up the grave old staircase (cautioned of the steps I knew so well), into the unchanged drawing-room. The books that Agnes and I had read together, were on their shelves; and the desk where I had laboured at my lessons, many a night, stood yet at the same old corner of the table. All the little changes that had crept in when the Heeps were there, were changed again. Everything was as it used to be, in the happy time.", "sha256": "c339f9ec8510264f4ecd6981a4bbf9c6ebba6ffe26c43c4b700cbeb2b380137e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[67]/p[29]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u062-b0030", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I stood in a window, and looked across the ancient street at the opposite houses, recalling how I had watched them on wet afternoons, when I first came there; and how I had used to speculate about the people who appeared at any of the windows, and had followed them with my eyes up and down stairs, while women went clicking along the pavement in pattens, and the dull rain fell in slanting lines, and poured out of the water-spout yonder, and flowed into the road. The feeling with which I used to watch the tramps, as they came into the town on those wet evenings, at dusk, and limped past, with their bundles drooping over their shoulders at the ends of sticks, came freshly back to me; fraught, as then, with the smell of damp earth, and wet leaves and briar, and the sensation of the very airs that blew upon me in my own toilsome journey.", "sha256": "e06341051bbb855774cf3746af2fa61f015eaf00fc8eb1b274d8f5e8de6a36ee", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[67]/p[30]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u062-b0031", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "The opening of the little door in the panelled wall made me start and turn. Her beautiful serene eyes met mine as she came towards me. She stopped and laid her hand upon her bosom, and I caught her in my arms.", "sha256": "0ae54d6dc6e1de8889c368597bd0887189a3f48a68dbb4db5cc61b0262c78431", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[67]/p[31]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}]}
